- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates prices; increase early forecast values, especially for first 5–7 days.
- Model consistently overreacts to sentiment spikes — if sentiment jumps to 1.00, forecast often overshoots by 20–40% in next 3–5 days; apply dampening factor to high sentiment periods.
- Forecast mean reversion is weak — model fails to decay toward historical mean after 10–15 days; apply exponential decay or moving average smoothing to later forecast days.
- For 30d horizon, model often overpredicts early days (1–7) and underpredicts late days (25–30) — adjust for asymmetric decay: reduce early forecast, increase late forecast only if sentiment remains positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model underestimates prices; add 10–20% buffer to early forecast to compensate for downward bias.
